answer.rationale: a glance-able live dashboard should update near-instantly without idle cost; polling wastes forks when the tree sits untouched between agent turns

rejected.why_not: wastes cycles/forks when idle, laggy at long intervals
defeats the point of a live dashboard

answer.text:
file-watch the store, re-run hydra resume on change
Watch .hydra/<slug>.json (and its lockfile) for write events; debounce against the lock's rename/write dance so a mid-write state never triggers a refresh.

concurrency.question: What happens when the TUI and an agent both touch the same tree at once (lockfile contention, live reload)?

answer.rationale: CLI JSON output is the stable interface hydra already exposes to agents; a read-only viewer has no reason to couple to internal Rust types or the on-disk format

rejected.why_not: couples build to internal crate boundaries, same-workspace requirement
duplicates hydra read logic, breaks silently on format change

answer.text:
shell out to hydra CLI subprocess
Same JSON interface an agent uses; re-invoked on refresh trigger (poll/watch settled under concurrency).

data-access.question: How does the TUI read tree state — shell out to the hydra CLI, or link hydra-core as a library?

answer.rationale: data-access already settled on CLI subprocess + JSON, not shared Rust types, so no code-sharing reason to force one binary; same workspace gets lean CLI deps without inventing a version-compat matrix between two independently-released things

rejected.why_not: forces ratatui/crossterm as transitive deps on every CLI user, ties TUI release cadence to CLI
no enforced pairing between TUI and CLI JSON schema versions

answer.text:
separate binary, same cargo workspace
Two [[bin]] targets, one Cargo.toml workspace, built/released from the same commit — schema drift between hydra and hydra-tui structurally impossible.

distribution.question: Is the TUI a subcommand of the hydra binary, or a separate crate/binary?

answer.rationale: file-watch already expects to hit hydra mid-write/lock-held routinely as normal operation, not fatal; last-good render should stay visible through a transient hiccup

rejected.why_not: blocks the last-good view exactly when something is wrong with the connection to it
throws away the dashboard over a transient lock/mid-write hiccup a watcher should tolerate

answer.text:
inline status line, TUI stays up
Persistent status line shows last error (tree gone, lock busy, subprocess not found); last-good render stays on screen underneath.

error-display.question: How do hydra CLI failures (exit 5 tree gone, exit 1 I/O/lock, subprocess not found) surface in the TUI?

answer.rationale: shares hydra own toolchain (cargo, repo, build); no second language install just to parse a JSON stream a subprocess already emits

rejected.why_not: second toolchain, no shared code with a Rust CLI
second toolchain plus a runtime dep the CLI user does not otherwise need

answer.text:
Rust + ratatui
crossterm backend, serde for JSON parsing of hydra subprocess output.

framework.question: What language/toolkit builds the TUI (e.g. ratatui, given hydra itself is a Rust binary)?

answer.rationale: prior/cauterised_by already come free in hydra show output; a passive dashboard earns its keep over raw CLI by surfacing that trail without an extra keypress or a second hydra show call

rejected.why_not: hides the why-did-this-change trail the skill relies on
extra keybinding and two-state pane for data that costs nothing extra to show

answer.text:
full history pane by default
Detail pane for a selected row shows current answer plus prior (pre-reopen) and cauterised_by, as a small timeline, no extra keypress needed.

history-view.question: Is there a view for prior/cauterised/reopened history, or only the current head state?

answer.rationale: scope settled read-only; there is no answer path in the TUI for this question to apply to.

interaction.question: If interactive, how does the user answer a head (inline form vs shelling to $EDITOR for prose fields)?

answer.rationale: covers which tree to open without committing to the extra complexity of multiple concurrent watchers/subprocess state a live switcher would need

rejected.option: single tree per launch via CLI arg
rejected.why_not: no discoverability, has to already know the slug
solves juggling several concurrent interviews, a problem that has not come up in this design

answer.text:
tree picker on launch, single tree per session
Opens on hydra trees list; Enter drills into chosen tree. Switching trees means quitting and relaunching.

multi-tree.question: Can the TUI switch between multiple trees, and how are they listed?

answer.rationale: terminal-tool audience already expects vim keys; fold/expand earns its keep on a real dozen-plus-head tree where an answered branch is noise once settled

rejected.why_not: same structural cost as vim-tree, worse fit for the likely audience
no way to collapse an answered branch, gets noisy on a large tree

answer.text:
vim-style keys (j/k/g/G/search), foldable tree rows
Collapse/expand state tracked per parent row; indent/nesting comes from the JSON skeleton's parent field.

navigation.question: What is the navigation/keybinding model (vim-style vs arrows, tree vs flat list)?

answer.rationale: JSON is needed anyway for selection state and file-watch diffing; building rows on top of it avoids a second tree-renderer drifting from the CLI ASCII rules

rejected.why_not: no per-row selection or scroll-to-node
duplicates CLI drawing rules, risks drift

answer.text:
JSON-driven selectable rows, reusing the CLI's own glyphs/labels
Parse hydra resume's skeleton into rows; keep each row's status glyph and summary text verbatim from the JSON rather than re-deriving them.

render-model.question: How is the tree rendered — reuse the `hydra tree` ASCII output, or a custom graph widget?

answer.rationale: agent-crafted options + rationale before every cut is core to the interview protocol; a TUI form cannot fake that judgment well, and a second mutation path complicates reopened[] cascades

rejected.why_not: TUI would recreate cut-time option/tradeoff judgment poorly
adds a second mutation path to reason about for cascades

answer.text:
read-only dashboard
Agent/CLI stays the only writer; TUI is eyes on the tree only.

scope.question: What does the TUI let a user do — read-only dashboard, or full interactive answer/cut/sprout?

answer.rationale: render layer is already JSON-driven (render-model), not subprocess-driven for visuals; TestBackend + fixture JSON tests exactly the state worth protecting (fold state, selection, history pane) without real file-watch timing flakiness

rejected.why_not: slower, flaky on real file-watch timing, exercises a path (subprocess spawn) with little design risk
enough state combinations (fold/selection/history/status-line) that regressions would go unnoticed

answer.text:
ratatui TestBackend + snapshot assertions
Render into in-memory buffer, feed synthetic key events, assert/diff buffer contents; fixture JSON stands in for hydra subprocess output.

testing.question: How is the TUI tested (snapshot testing, scripted key-sequences)?

answer.rationale: glyphs already carry the meaning; color is a scan-ability layer on top, no need for NO_COLOR/background-detection cross-cutting logic on a tool already correct without it

rejected.why_not: leaves scan-ability on the table for free
adds env detection and background sniffing for decoration, not information

answer.text:
fixed ANSI color scheme, no NO_COLOR/background detection
Color layered on top of existing glyphs for scan-ability (e.g. green=answered, yellow=blocked, red=cauterised); glyphs remain the source of truth.

theming.question: Is there a theme/color scheme, and does it respect terminal light/dark or NO_COLOR?
